column1: # ml-classify-table.tsv — the weighted feature table behind --ml-classify.
# WHAT THIS IS: a small linear model over flow statistics. Each row says "when
# feature F falls in bucket B, add W to the score of class C". Scoring a flow is
# the sum of the weights of the buckets its observed features fall in; the class
# with the highest sum wins and the runner-up is reported as the margin. A
# negative weight is evidence *against* a class (a TCP flow is not GTP-U), which
# is what keeps a sustained bulk transfer on port 80 from being called media.
# WHAT THIS IS NOT: a trained model. The weights are hand-set priors in the range
# -4..+4, written from published traffic-shape knowledge and the port and MTU
# anchors cited below, not fitted to a corpus and not validated against one. The
# table is data on purpose so a measured table can replace it without touching a
# module; a table fitted on labelled traffic is the honest upgrade, and until
# then a verdict from this table is a suggestion with a stated margin, never a
# DOCTRINE: a feature a flow does not carry is *unobserved*, not zero. The
# scorer names the features it used and the ones it could not, and refuses a
# verdict when fewer than MIN-OBSERVED are present.
# ── port (transport port registry; the scorer takes the lower of the two ports,
#    because an ephemeral client port is above 32768 — RFC 6335 §6 — so the
#    lower number is the service side) ──
# ── size_mean (mean IP datagram size; anchors are the smallest useful segment
#    128, a TLS record with its header 512, the 1024-octet small-buffer line and
#    the 1400-octet payload of a 1500-octet Ethernet frame — RFC 894 MTU minus
# ── rate_pps (packets per second; 1500-octet frames cap a 10 Mbit/s bearer near
#    812 pps, so >100 pps at MTU size is media or bulk and <0.5 pps is a
# ── size_cv (coefficient of variation of packet size, sigma/mu; a padded media
#    or tunnelled flow is flat, cv < 0.10 — the padded-cell observation that
#    makes page fingerprints weak on a mobile bearer) ──
# ── the two thresholds, kept in the table so a measured model can move them ──
# MIN-OBSERVED: a two-feature verdict on a six-feature model is a coin toss with
# a table attached; three is the floor at which a margin still means something.
# MIN-MARGIN: one weight step is noise, two is a preference; below it the
# verdict is reported as `weak` rather than `classified`.
# MIN-CONF: confidence is the winning score over the largest score these buckets
# could have produced, so a flow whose evidence is thin in absolute terms cannot
# be called classified on a margin alone.
